concerns.text: T006a mandates 'fail loudly' if fetch fails, halting execution. This contradicts the Plan's adopted strategy of manual curation (data/raw/nist_refs.json) and the Constitution's Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires the system to run on a fresh runner. A task that intentionally crashes on a missing API when the spec/plan explicitly allows manual curation is a semantic weakening of the requirement to 'obtain ground truth'.

Tasks T008a/b/c are defined as 'Spec Kickback' tasks *within* the execution artifact (tasks.md). This violates the separation of concerns: tasks.md describes implementation steps, not specification editing. An implementer cannot 'update spec.md' as a code task without a spec-change workflow. This creates a logical impossibility where the task cannot be completed as written, effectively weakening the requirement to align the spec with the plan.

T021 instructs the implementation to sweep regression start times at '[deferred], [deferred], [deferred]'. This is a semantic weakening of SC-003 and FR-005, which require a measurable outcome (sweeping {10%, 20%, 30%}). Executing code with literal '[deferred]' strings will cause a runtime crash or logic error, failing to deliver the required sensitivity analysis. The task must use the concrete values defined in the Plan (10%, 20%, 30%) or the [deferred] marker must be removed from the task description entirely.

T027 implements 'descriptive trend analysis' citing T008b, but the task description lacks the specific output format or threshold required to verify the 'done' state against the original intent of SC-005 (which was a statistical test). While the Plan notes the switch to trend analysis due to N=3, the task must explicitly define the output (e.g., 'report MAE reduction percentage') to prevent the deliverable from falling short of the verification requirement.
